clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. Sabrina exhibited a cheerful affect and was generally cooperative during the assessment. Upon evaluation, her muscle tone was noted to be within normal limits with a full range of motion. Her attention span was inconsistent, with notable distractibility interrupting task performance, requiring frequent verbal and visual redirection. Engagement with structured activities was variable; Sabrina responded more favorably to self-directed tasks, albeit with continued need for moderate verbal cues. Fine motor coordination displayed challenges, particularly in tasks that necessitated bilateral integration, where she occasionally required hand-over-hand assistance. Behavioral observations indicated that Sabrina needed a calm environment for optimal task focus, affecting the validity of standardized tests due to the need for environmental and procedural adaptations.
